_meta.purpose: A PUBLIC map of CLINICAL ACTION THRESHOLDS. These are NOT reference intervals. A reference interval is the central 95 % of the values of a healthy population, that is, statistics; an action threshold is derived from outcomes and decisions, and it regularly lies INSIDE the reference corridor (prediabetes at HbA1c 5.7 with a laboratory norm up to 6.0) or far BEYOND it (haematocrit 54 % on testosterone therapy with a laboratory ceiling of 49). That is exactly why a position inside the corridor is almost uninterpretable, while a threshold is interpretable.
_meta.schema: marker → a list of thresholds. value — the value in the units of labs.json; side — which side the threshold is on (high: value ≥ value; low: value ≤ value); label — what it means; source — where it comes from; action — what is done clinically; applies_when_class — the threshold applies only if the regimen contains a drug of that class (otherwise the threshold is a general one).
_meta.disclaimer: The thresholds are a reason for a question to the doctor, not a command. The assistant does not change therapy.
_meta.applies_to: THE MECHANISM FOR LIMITING THRESHOLDS. The machine field is `applies_when_class`: the engine skips such a threshold if the user has no active drug of that class (this is how haematocrit 54 % is counted only on testosterone therapy). The `applies_to` field is a HUMAN-READABLE mark for the cases a drug class does not express; the engine does NOT execute it, and it must not be put in place of `applies_when_class`. If a limitation by sex is ever needed, an `applies_when_sex` field is added together with two lines in `_thresholds_for` next to the class check — otherwise the field is decoration rather than a rule. The absence of any of these fields means «the threshold applies to adults in general»: most of them are derived from outcomes and do not depend on sex or age.
